title: Cross-precision FlashAttention prober and decode-jitter smoothing
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Investigate and implement a lightweight cross-precision kernel prober and a decode-scheduling jitter smoothing shim to safely integrate FlashAttention v2/v3 variants across precision modes (FP16/FP8/int8-like quantizations). Goal: reduce tail latency regressions observed when the runtime switches kernels during decode, and provide an automated, low-risk canary path for rolling FAv3 variants into production.
background: Recent canary runs for FAv3 on our baseline Llama-family workloads showed occasional 99th percentile latency spikes during decode when the kernel selector switches between FP16-optimized and quantized paths mid-request. These spikes are correlated with head-slicing and long-prefix cache warmups. Existing profilers provide per-kernel aggregates, but lack a lightweight in-flight probe that measures cross-precision execution cost and memory working set at typical request sizes. We need an operational prober + a decode jitter mitigation layer that is cheap to enable for canaries and protective in prod.
proposal: 1) Implement a Cross-Precision Kernel Prober (CPKP): a short, synthetic micro-workload dispatched to candidate kernels just prior to a staged rollout. CPKP will measure: effective latency for short decode windows, peak workspace allocation, and KV-cache touch patterns. 2) Add a decode-jitter smoothing shim that limits kernel switches within a configurable time window per-request (default 50ms) and optionally pins decode for the first N tokens to the initial kernel choice. 3) Expose prober metrics and a canary pipeline: if CPKP shows <5% median delta and <10% 99th delta vs baseline, allow staged canary; otherwise auto-fallback to stable kernel. 4) Add end-to-end e2e regression tests in the runtime test harness and a perf dashboard for canary runs.
tasks: Design CPKP micro-workload and measurement signals (latency, alloc, kv-touch) - ownership: runtime/attn-team
Implement lightweight prober with configurable target kernels and duration - ETA 3d
Implement decode-jitter smoothing shim: time-window and token-pin policies - ETA 2d
Wire prober + shim into canary flow and feature flag (ff:cross_precision_prober) - DevOps collaboration
Add e2e perf tests to runtime CI harness and create synthetic suite reflecting head-slicing & long-prefix scenarios
Dashboard: add CPKP metrics, canary pass/fail, and per-kernel latency histograms to Console (redwood-console#perf/cross-precision)
Run internal canary against dedicated pool and validate with traffic replay and golden prompt set
acceptance_criteria: CPKP can run in under 120ms and report median/99th latency + peak workspace without impacting live decode streams
Decode-jitter smoothing prevents more than one kernel switch per-request inside the smoothing window; default policy reduces observed 99th tail spikes by >=20% on replayed failing traces
Automated canary gate uses CPKP thresholds and prevents rollout if 99th delta >10% or peak workspace > baseline *1.25
CI includes an e2e regression test that reproduces the previously observed FAv3 decode spike and asserts the smoothing shim mitigates it
Documentation: short runbook in Confluence describing how to interpret prober results and how to revert canary (link included)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Prober itself could perturb allocator state leading to false positives. Mitigation: run prober with isolated workspace allocator and a short cool-down between probe and real traffic
Risk: Smoothing window may add steady-state latency for short requests. Mitigation: default config pins only for first N tokens (e.g., 8) and uses a short time window; evaluate tradeoff on p50/p95
Risk: Probe thresholds tuned on synthetic workloads might not generalize. Mitigation: gather data from a diverse prompt corpus and include production replay traces in canaries

2025-02-24: Early CPKP prototype measured peak workspace within 10% of baseline in 90% of runs; some outliers observed on multi-tenant nodes
